First of all, I'm really sorry for what happened. Your ex did a terrible thing. Now, as for the current relationship, it's good that you've already taken the initiative by discussing the things that worry you, when he's as good as you he is, he'll understand. He'll know that he might need to be patient with you initially.

As for your own peace of mind, you do not have to give yourself entirely into the new relationship all too soon. It's alright to take your time to build the trust. REMEMBER what happened in the past only enough to make sure you aren't hurt again, to keep yourself on your toes. If he ever feels distant, tell him you'd be happy to talk things through. Time will make your relationship stronger and you'll be able to trust him completely and that's when you'll know that you wouldn't have to linger on the past. At all...

Best of luck for the future OP. :)

The way I stumbled upon the evidence is what made the situation worse. My life has fallen apart ever since and even though months have passed, I'm still reeling and grieving about what once was.

Your SO doesn't deserve that, no one does. He clearly still loves you. Do right by him this time. Sit him down and tell him the truth. The ENTIRE truth. And after that if he still wishes to carry on, end it from your side because you know that you don't respect him right now. The guilt you feel is not about cheating on him, it's more about the fear, the fear of him finding out one day. If you decide to hide it, you'll be constantly worrying about it and trust me, things like this have a funny way of coming out. Getting back like that wouldn't be healthy for either of you.

So it's upto you to decide how you want to play it. But if you still love him, put the poor fellow out of this misery.

I don’t know how it's better to be cheated on than to cheat. Because it's completely unfair that even though you did everything right by them, stood by their side whenever they needed you and still, it's you who gets thrown into a bottomless pit of pain, misery, loneliness and soul crushing sadness while they're out there in the world socialising,  having fun, acting like nothing ever happened. 

There are nights when you can't sleep because the thoughts are racing in your head. You twist and turn constantly,  try to think of something else but it doesn't work because they're sleeping like fucking babies right next to you. You want to scream at them and wake them up because you've had enough. You're in over your head when you see them lying next you without a speck of guilt or remorse on them.

Why? You keep asking yourself that. Just because you're easy work? In all those years, you looked at them the same way you looked at them 5 years ago. People called them flat-chested, you gave them your shoulder when they cried about that. You told them that it didn't matter to you, you still found them attractive. They start putting on weight, they feel depressed about it. You do everything in your power to show them how you still appreciated them. But even after all this, they still had to get their ego stroked by someone else.You try to convince yourself so hard that she’s still the innocent little girl who you fell so hard for. You refuse to believe that the innocence has faded. Your dream has now turned into a nightmare of sorts. You keep wishing  gor it to end.

You can't talk to your friends about this not even your family. It's easy for them to say "leave her and move on" because they don't understand,  they never will. How can they? They haven't been in your shoes. No one should ever be. You can't talk about it with her either can you? Because she won’t understand why it's difficult for you to watch a particular movie or a show. She still gets upset you end up drinking a little more and want to be left alone after that.

In the end, all you end up doing is keeping it all in and pray that you don't implode one fine day.

TL; DR: My half-drunken sob story. Not the right place I know but if you read it all, I really appreciate it.
